svg.title: Inside a segment
svg.desc: A segment holds sorted distinct hash keys, an open-addressing directory from hash to run whose 12-byte slots hold the key, the run's 40-bit start, its length and its largest per-reference multiplicity, and the references and times of every posting bit-packed to the width of the largest value. A run is grouped by reference with times ascending.
svg.text: Postings sorted by (hash, reference, time), never changed once built: sorted keys, a directory from hash to run, packed postings.
keys the sorted distinct hashes, u32, 4 bytes each
Merges and iteration in key order
walk these; no offsets array is
directory open addressing with linear probing, at most 3 keys per 5 slots; rebuilt from the keys, never stored
0x3fa1c2e0: home slot 5 is taken, so the probe moves on to 6
× slots ≫ 32. A lookup is one read,
one slot, 12 bytes slot 6, holding the run of 0x3fa1c2e0
The hash itself; a probe stops at
its own key or at an empty slot.
The run's first posting. With start hi it is
40 bits: a segment holds under 2⁴⁰ postings.
refs and times one value per posting, each array packed to the bits of its largest value
run of 0x3fa1c2e0: the slot's start 1,204 and len 7
references ascend through the run; mult = 3 (reference 7)
How 17-bit references sit in bytes (little-endian, least significant bit first)
Reading value i is one unaligned 8-byte load at byte ⌊17i / 8⌋, a shift right by 17i mod 8, and a 17-bit mask.
Eight slack bytes after the array keep every such load inside it.
With simd on an AVX2 CPU, a block of eight values (17 bytes at this width) decodes at once: one byte
shuffle, one variable shift and one mask, for widths up to 25 bits.
